newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Ras Tanura oil refinery upgrade delayed - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Ras Tanura oil refinery upgrade delayed - MEES.

text.p: Saudi Aramco's Ras Tanura oil refinery upgrade program has been delayed to at least the second quarter of 1998, the Cyprus-based Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) newsletter reported on Monday.
"Commissioning of the $1.5 billion Ras Tanura refinery upgrading program appears to have been set back at least until the second quarter of 1998, and possibly beyond," MEES reported.

The upgrading program, which will raise throughput at the Aramco refinery to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) from 265,000 bpd and boost middle distillate and gasoline yields, had been expected to come on stream in the first quarter of next year.
MEES gave no reason for the start-up delay.

Work on the plant involves installing a 40,000 bpd hydrocracker, a 40,000 bpd continuous catalytic reformer, a 60,000 bpd vis-breaker, a 65 million cubic feet a day hydrogen plant, a hydrogen purification unit, a 55,000 bpd naphtha hydrotreater, sulfur recovery and sour water treatment units.
The catalytic reformer would ease tight domestic gasoline supplies while additional gas oil output would help free up volumes for export.
